They were cells in the body of a sprawling, malevolent mass.
The Sentients had been given a mandate to evolve, and their only model for the endpoint of such evolution was us.
Transcript: We did not think of the Sentients as a ‘them’ so much as an ‘it’.
VM: SENTIENCE
They were returning to the Origin System not just to obliterate the Orokin, but to replace them and ultimately… perfect them.
We were, I think, too conditioned by our experiences with the Infestation - a hive-mind of quite a different order.
We faced legions hurled at us with no more regard for their individual lives than corpuscles have.
It was easily done. I was too glorious a figure to be suspected
Transcript: Among the Seven I was - so I was told - considered Nitokh’s plaything and concubine.
The blood of better men dappled me like medals. In secret I amassed weapons for Nitokh.
VM: COMMISSION
In the early days of the War they appointed me Vice Regent Grand Carnus at her goading, thinking it a jest.
How quickly their laughter turned to solemn applause as I brought home the news of one victory after another.
It was always the standard they still bore, glittering in its Orokin gold, and smeared in dappled crimson.
Transcript: Nothing quite speaks to the pomposity with which we creatures treat the carnage of war quite as succinctly as the bannermen.
Laughable though that is.
I always ensured it stood proud upon the field before I departed.
VM: STANDARD
Those who must be protected at all costs - and followed without question.
And who may be threatened, I might add, to follow orders that no sane soldier would ever complete, lest they somehow come to suffer some more terrible fate.
It was always their forms my eye was drawn to amongst the rest, though their mangled bodies were no different from any other.
Childhood friends now in charge of legions of Dax, of Grineer, null-matter cells, self-replicating carcinators, primitive biodrone blade-spiders, canisters of low-tech troops.
Transcript: I recall them now. Coteries of laughing Orokin youth.
Nobility clad in the as-yet-unspoiled raiments of command.
Golden boys and girls with ravening devils at their beck.
Their arrogance trickles like stinging sweat into my mind. They drank and sang, boasting of the times to come.
VM: COMMANDERS
They would make names for themselves. Raise their families high in honor.
So many of them fell. Not even their bodies were returned.
To prevent the enemy from gleaning our secrets, they were Kuva-jolted to liquefy upon death.
The hope of a generation turned to an oily puddle, sloshed through by Grineer boots.
